instruction: unlocked_waist: pick up the cup, place it into the drawer and close the drawer

calls.reason: Lower the left hand slightly toward the cup to establish visual joint response.
Bring the open left hand inward toward the cup.
Correct inward alignment from the observed shoulder-yaw response.
Advance the open left hand beside the cup and turn the wrist for contact.
Close the left fingers gradually around the cup.
Reopen slightly and center the left palm nearer the cup.
Rotate the left hand around its approach axis to improve finger placement at the cup.
Close the aligned hand around the cup.
Make a small lateral correction while maintaining a gentle grasp attempt.
Lift slightly to test whether the cup is secured.
Move the raised hand slightly sideways to reveal whether the cup follows.
Reopen and lower the left hand, angling the fingers toward the cup for a deeper grasp.
Lower the open hand further toward the cup's body using shoulder and elbow position.
Advance the lowered hand to put the cup between the palm and fingers.
Close around the cup after visible contact at the lower hand position.
Allow the fingers to settle around the cup before lifting.
Lift the closed hand gently and check the cup's motion.
Open and rotate the left wrist to approach the cup with the palm facing it.
Place the open, turned hand over the cup with fingers straddling its body.
Lower into contact and close the fingers and opposing thumb around the cup.
Settle the opposing thumb while maintaining the cup contact.
Test the revised grasp with a small upward movement.
Check cup retention with a small movement toward the drawer.
Reposition the open palm farther over the cup before closing again.
Center the cup beneath the open palm and thumb.
Enclose the cup at the centered position.
Let the fingers finish closing before the retention test.
Lift and shift the grasp slightly to test whether the cup is carried.
Angle the open fingers downward and lower the hand closer to the cup.
Move the open hand back slightly so the finger closing region aligns with the cup.
Close around the cup at its observed new position near the thumb.
Maintain the grasp briefly to settle finger contact.
Complete the finger closure around the displaced cup.
Lift the tightened grasp slowly to test cup retention.
Shift the raised hand slightly toward the drawer to verify the cup follows.
Reopen and approach the cup from its near side at the new table position.
Position the thumb beside the cup while keeping the fingers open.
Align the fingers on the far side of the cup and the thumb on its near side.
Close the opposing thumb and fingers around the visible cup body.
Increase finger closure to secure the cup between thumb and fingers.
Lift the newly closed grasp while checking the cup remains within the fingers.
Check cup retention by moving the raised hand away from the original cup location.
Lower the open hand to the cup's height after the retention test showed it stayed on the table.
Shift the lowered hand over the cup while keeping the grasp open.
Reposition behind the cup near the table edge without closing against it.
Close around the cup from its near side at the edge position.
Make a small waist adjustment to improve the view of the cup near the table edge.
Restore a view of the near table edge and inspect the lifted hand.
Bring the lifted hand into the camera view to inspect whether the cup is held.
Lift and bring the closed hand centrally into view for inspection and possible transfer.
Move the closed hand toward the drawer opening while keeping it raised.
Advance the raised hand over the drawer opening.
Clear the drawer front and position the hand over its interior.
Center the hand over the drawer interior before opening it.
Open the hand over the drawer and inspect for the cup.
Withdraw the open hand to inspect the drawer and table for the cup.
Look farther down toward the near table edge to locate the cup.
Inspect the left near edge where the cup was last visible.
Clear the hand from the last seen area and inspect the table edge below it.
Inspect farther along the near left table edge to locate the displaced cup.
Change the viewing angle at the near left edge without reaching into the unseen area.
Inspect the left side of the table for the displaced cup.
Lower the open left hand outside the table edge toward the visible floor object.
Extend the left arm downward beside the table while tracking the floor object.
Bend at the waist and advance the lowered arm toward the floor object's position.
Lower the shoulder and advance the open hand toward the floor object while staying outside the table.
Align the extended hand with the visible floor object using small shoulder adjustments.
Move the hand outward from the table edge before continuing the floor approach.
Lower the open hand slightly at the floor object while preserving clearance from the table edge.
Make a small alignment and begin closing around the floor object's position.
Complete the gentle closure at the last visible object position before lifting for inspection.
Lift slightly and improve visibility to test the floor grasp.
Bring the raised hand fully into view to inspect whether the floor object follows.
Test retention with a small outward hand movement while holding the grasp closed.
Reopen and lower the extended hand for a closer floor approach, keeping it left of the table edge.
Allow the lowered open hand to settle before the next small alignment.
Angle the fingers toward the floor object and align the grasp region with it.
Close the lowered, angled fingers at the floor object.
Lift the closed hand from the floor area and inspect for retention.
Check whether the cup moves with the lifted hand.
Withdraw the empty hand upward and away from the floor and table edge before stopping.
Finish raising the torso with the left arm clear of the table edge.
